detailed_summary: This paper reports the first demonstration of optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in a II-VI semiconductor, specifically chlorine donors in ZnSe. The authors leverage spin-selective donor-bound exciton (DBX) transitions to initialize the electron spin and directly resolve spin-relaxation dynamics. Coherent control is achieved using off-resonant picosecond optical pulses, evidenced by spin Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference. Furthermore, by coherently driving two spin-selective optical transitions, they observe high-contrast coherent population trapping (CPT), forming an optically controlled dark state. At higher driving strengths, multiple dark resonances emerge, revealing the hyperfine interaction between the electron spin and the I=3/2 Cl nucleus. The work establishes isolated optical donors in ZnSe as a promising platform for solid-state optically active qubits, combining bright optical transitions with long-lived spin coherence and complete coherent control.

It advances the development of optically active spin qubits in semiconductors, a key component for scalable quantum networks. The demonstration of coherent control and CPT in a II-VI material system opens new avenues for studying light-matter interaction at the single-spin level.
